blocking.section: Observability principles (aggregates and sharding) / Cardinality and overhead budgets (Overhead per signal)
blocking.issue: Still unresolved from the last round. The rule for which families shard still goes by label kind rather than by how many requests reach a label set. Gateway-scoped Policies reach every Route: the Configuration model worked example has five, `cors-default`, `jwt-default`, `ratelimit-global`, `headers-security` and `geo-block-default`. Every request on the Node therefore records into the same `ruralz_filter_duration_seconds{policy, phase}` label sets. In the SM-4 reference scenario, and on any Node dominated by one Route, every request also records into the same `ruralz_http_requests_total{route}` and `ruralz_http_request_duration_seconds{route}` label sets. Under the current rule these are 'other label sets' and get one unpadded atomic per value. At 32 P every core bounces the same bucket, `_count` and `_sum` cache lines. A cross-core line transfer costs about 100 ns (hypothesis), while the 2 µs budget for 40 operations leaves 50 ns per operation. The document also never says how a histogram `_sum` in seconds is added atomically. Go has no atomic float add, so a float64 sum needs a compare-and-swap retry loop, and that loop gets worse under contention. The contention the sharding was meant to remove therefore stays in the scenario where the Metrics row, SLO-GW-2 and SLO-GW-3 are measured.
blocking.evidence: Observability principles: "Only hot families shard: listener-scoped and enumeration-only families, at most 1,000 counter or gauge series and 64 histogram label sets (target), into S = min(`GOMAXPROCS` at start, 8) shards (target) padded to 64-byte cache lines." and "Other label sets use one unpadded atomic per value." Overhead per signal: "| Metrics | 2 µs or less (target) | 0 (target) | 24 MiB or less (target) |" and "15 metric operations in the SM-4 scenario and 40 for 10 Filters".
blocking.fix: Define hot by reach, not by label kind. Also shard the label sets of Gateway-scoped Policies, which are bounded by Gateway Policies × Phases, and the Route counter and histogram label sets of the first N admitted Routes (target). A simpler alternative is to shard every label set of the `fast` histogram families. Store histogram `_sum` as an integer count of nanoseconds or bytes, updated with `atomic.AddUint64`, and convert it at export. Add these shards to the metrics memory model, for example 2,000 Route histogram label sets × 192 bytes × 8 shards ≈ 3 MiB at S = 8 (hypothesis), then recompute the Metrics and All telemetry rows. Make the M1 contention benchmark run one hot Route with Gateway Policies at 32 P.

blocking.issue: Still unresolved from the last round. The 32-interval cap cannot hold on ordinary traffic. Blocked body reads and client writes are excluded intervals, but copy work between them stays gateway-added. So in a pass-through copy, adjacent intervals never touch and never merge, and each chunk adds about two intervals. Any unary response of more than about 16 chunks (roughly 512 KiB at 32 KiB reads), and any trickling Upstream, goes over 32. Those requests are 'skipped and counted' and drop out of `ruralz_http_gateway_duration_seconds`. The SLIs of SLO-GW-2 and SLO-GW-3 then lean toward small bodies, and `interval_overflow` fills on normal traffic. Separately, parallel `aggregate` legs insert intervals from different goroutines into one pooled buffer, and the document does not say how that stays race-free without a lock on the request path.
blocking.evidence: Gateway-added time: "`ruralz_http_gateway_duration_seconds` is wall-clock time minus the union of excluded intervals: client reads and writes, upstream I/O, State Store round trips and declared remote calls (pack 8.7 rule 6)." and "Upstream I/O is time blocked on the Upstream (pooled-connection wait, dial, TLS, awaiting headers, blocked body reads and writes); Filters and copy work during a leg stay gateway-added. Intervals merge on insert, so parallel `aggregate` legs count once; a request keeps at most 32 (target) in a pooled buffer, beyond which it is skipped and counted."
blocking.fix: Replace the interval list with a constant-size accumulator. Keep a per-request excluded-depth counter and a timestamp. Each blocked section increments the depth on entry and decrements it on exit, and time is added to the excluded total only on the 0-to-1 and 1-to-0 transitions. That gives an exact union for sequential and parallel legs, uses per-request atomics and needs no cap. Then drop `ruralz_http_gateway_duration_skipped_total`, or keep it only for clock anomalies. If a list is kept, use it only for parallel composition and plain sums for sequential sections, because one goroutine's blocked sections never overlap.

blocking.section: Cardinality and overhead budgets (Overhead per signal, metrics memory model)
blocking.issue: Still unresolved from the last round. The metrics memory model budgets exactly one collection of live heap, but the budget is RSS and nothing bounds concurrent collections. By the document's own figures, the collection term (125,000 × 120 bytes ≈ 15 MB) is about two thirds of the 22.6 MiB. The OTLP periodic reader and every `/metrics` scraper each materialize one. An HA pair of Prometheus servers, the OTLP reader and an ad hoc curl can overlap, and each overlap adds about 15 MB, so memory grows with the number of scrapers. Also, 'Memory is RSS', but the arithmetic sums live bytes. With the default GOGC=100 and no GOMEMLIMIT, the heap target is about twice live heap, and collection output is short-lived garbage. About 23 MiB of live metrics state can therefore show as up to about 46 MiB of RSS. The 24 MiB Metrics row and the 40 MiB All telemetry row cannot be met as written.
blocking.evidence: Overhead per signal: "Memory is RSS above the 96 MiB idle budget (target) in [Tech stack and libraries](../engineering/01-tech-stack-and-libraries.md) (OQ-observability-17)." and "Metrics memory, checked by an M1 heap and contention benchmark at 4 P and 32 P, assumes 120 bytes per counter or gauge series and 300 per histogram label set, 64 × S and 192 × S more when sharded, and 120 per exported series in a collection (hypothesis). At the Node limit of 125,000 series, half histogram buckets, the unsharded part is about 22.6 MiB". Observability principles: "read by both exporters".
blocking.fix: Allow at most one collection in flight per process. Use single-flight so that concurrent scrapes share one encoded result, cached for up to 1 s (target), and have the OTLP reader either reuse that result or wait for it. A better option is to stream-encode `/metrics` straight from the aggregates into a bounded pooled buffer, so a collection costs a fixed buffer instead of 120 bytes per series. Then state the memory figures either as live heap times an explicit RSS factor, or under a documented GOMEMLIMIT or GOGC setting that the M1 benchmark uses. Recompute both rows and OQ-observability-17 to match.

blocking.section: Logging and access logs (Access logs) / Cardinality and overhead budgets (Overhead per signal)
blocking.issue: Still unresolved from the last round. The access-log queue memory budget contradicts the record size the document allows. 4 MiB for 8,192 records is 512 bytes per record, yet `host` and `path` alone may take 256 + 1,024 = 1,280 bytes. On top of that come a `User-Agent` with no stated length, names, IDs, the `failure_modes` list and the `ai` object. A burst of long-path requests fills the queue at about 1.5 KiB or more per record, 12 MiB or more in total. That is three times the row and pushes All telemetry past 40 MiB. If pooled records instead reference request strings rather than copying them, each queued record keeps its request's header block alive, up to the 256 KiB process ceiling in Data plane, which is far worse.
blocking.evidence: Access log fields: "| `method`, `host`, `path`, `truncated` | No query string; `host` and `path` cut at 256 and 1,024 bytes (target), flagged in `truncated` |" and "| `user_agent`, `tls_version` | Truncated `User-Agent`; TLS version |". Overhead per signal: "| Access log, logged request | 2 µs or less at p99, `when` included (target) | 8 or fewer (target) | 8,192-record queue, 4 MiB or less (target) |". Access logs: "The request goroutine evaluates `when` and fills a pooled record for a worker to encode; a full queue drops with a counter."
blocking.fix: Bound the queue by bytes as well as by records. Reserve each record's actual size from a 4 MiB (target) byte budget and drop with `reason="queue_full"` when the budget is exhausted. Records MUST copy truncated fields into their own pooled buffer and never reference request memory. Give `User-Agent` a length, for example 256 bytes (target), and cap `failure_modes` and the `ai` object. Alternatively, keep a record count only and set the memory row to 8,192 × the maximum record size.

blocking.issue: Still unresolved from the last round. Folding a retiring label set into `_overflow` together with its accumulated value creates increments that never happened. When the retiring ceiling is hit, a counter or histogram that has accumulated, say, 10 million requests or 5,000 5xx disappears, and `_overflow` jumps by that amount in one step. `rate()` and `increase()` over `_overflow`, and every `sum(rate(...))` panel over the family, then show a spike of events that never occurred in that window. SLO SLIs on per-resource families can fold this way. SLO-GW-4 reads `ruralz_plugin_call_overhead_seconds{policy, phase}`, and SLO-AI-1 sums over `provider` and `model`, so the spike feeds burn-rate rules and can page falsely. The claim that SLO SLIs never fold covers only listener and enumeration families, which is not true of these two.
blocking.evidence: Cardinality budget: "A Node-wide ceiling of 25,000 retiring series (target) caps a Node at 125,000 series: beyond it the oldest retiring sets fold into `_overflow`, values and late records included; per-Revision admission ignores retiring sets, so live folding stays identical on every Node." and "Listener and enumeration families, including SLO SLIs, are admitted first and never fold." SLO definitions: "| SLO-GW-4 | `ruralz_plugin_call_overhead_seconds` bucket `le=\"0.00005\"` / `_count` |" and "| SLO-AI-1 | 1 − M / (`ruralz_ai_settlements_total` + M) ... both summed over `provider` and `model` |".
blocking.fix: When a retiring set folds, end its series: stop exporting it and let OTLP and Prometheus staleness close it. Send only records that arrive after the fold to `_overflow`, and never carry accumulated values over. Apply the same rule when a Hot Reload moves a live label set past an admission limit. Then correct 'including SLO SLIs' to name which SLI families can fold, or make SLO-GW-4 and SLO-AI-1 read families that never fold.

blocking.section: Control plane observability / Grafana dashboards and SLOs (Alert rules)
blocking.issue: Still unresolved from the last round. Page-severity rules built on `increase()` over rare-event counters miss the first event, and the document claims the opposite. A counter series first created at 1 has no earlier sample, so `increase()` returns 0 and the page never fires. Examples are the first failed Rollout since the leader started and the first `RZ-CFG-027` NACK. L counters restart on every failover as new series from a different replica (`service.instance.id` changes), so a failure shortly after a leader change is lost the same way. `RuralzRolloutFailed` (page), the NACK half of `RuralzTampering` (page) and `RuralzAIProviderCredential` all depend on events that are rare by nature. The document never says that alerted label sets exist at 0 before their first event.
blocking.evidence: Control plane observability: "L counters restart with a new start time after failover, which `rate()` and `increase()` tolerate, so nothing extra reaches Raft;". Alert rules: "expr: max by (cluster) (increase(ruralz_control_rollouts_total{state=\"failed\"}[15m])) > 0" with "labels: {severity: page}", and "max by (cluster) (increase(ruralz_control_nacks_total{code=\"RZ-CFG-027\"}[1h])) > 0" with "labels: {severity: page}".
blocking.fix: Require every enumeration label set that an alert rule references to be created at 0 before the first event: at process start, and for L series when leadership is acquired. That covers the `state` and `kind` values, the `error_class` values, and the registry `code` values the rules use. Add a CI test that each alerted series exists at 0 after start and after failover. Alternatively, alert on the gauges that hold these states (for example `ruralz_control_rollout_state_info{state="failed"}`) and keep `increase()` for dashboards. Restate the `rate()` and `increase()` sentence with this precondition.

blocking.section: Metrics catalog (Ruralz Gateway metrics, Degraded states)
blocking.issue: Still unresolved from the last round, plus one new omission. The document says it accepts other documents' proposed names, but the catalog and the fixed O3 `reason` set leave out or contradict four sibling proposals. CI 'fails on a panel using an unlisted metric', so it rejects signals the sibling designs rely on. (1) Traffic management and resilience proposes `ruralz_upstream_probes_skipped_total` and degraded reason `probes_skipped`; neither appears here. (2) Multi-protocol proposes `ruralz_ingress_hold_expiries_total`, which is missing. (3) Traffic management and resilience gives `ruralz_cache_store_skipped_total` the reason `state_store_memory`, while this catalog and the failure-matrix paragraph use `memory`. (4) New: Data plane says a snapshot still pinned after the ending bound 'stays ending as a degraded state, never freed early'. The loader then activates no newer Revision until that snapshot is freed, so every later Hot Reload is blocked. No `ruralz_node_degraded_info` reason and no alert covers this state, which breaks O3 and P10 for one of the most consequential stuck states on a Node.
blocking.evidence: Ruralz Gateway metrics: "Other documents' proposed names are accepted, renaming [Traffic management and resilience](09-traffic-management-and-resilience.md)'s `ruralz_upstream_endpoint_ejections_total` to `ruralz_upstream_ejections_total`." and "| `ruralz_cache_store_skipped_total` | Counter | stores | `policy`, `reason` | size_limit, buffer_budget, memory |". Traffic management and resilience: "skipped probes count in `ruralz_upstream_probes_skipped_total` and, above 10% for 1 minute, raise degraded reason `probes_skipped` (target), both proposed to Observability" and "`ruralz_cache_store_skipped_total` reasons are `size_limit`, `buffer_budget` and `state_store_memory`." Multi-protocol: "letting `AckWait` redeliver (`ruralz_ingress_hold_expiries_total`, proposed)". Data plane: "a snapshot pinned longer stays ending as a degraded state, never freed early" and "The loader keeps only the latest pending Revision and activates it once that snapshot is freed". Degraded states table: no reason for a stuck ending snapshot or for skipped probes.
blocking.fix: Add the missing rows: `ruralz_upstream_probes_skipped_total` (Counter, probes, `upstream`, Planned (M1)) and `ruralz_ingress_hold_expiries_total` (Counter, holds, `route`, `protocol`, Planned (M4)). Add `probes_skipped` to Degraded states. Add a degraded reason such as `snapshot_retirement_stuck`, raised while a snapshot stays ending past the Data plane bound, and give it a page or ticket rule, since Hot Reload is blocked while it lasts. Pick one cache skip reason: `state_store_memory` matches the degraded-reason naming. Use it in the table and in the failure-matrix sentence, and record the choice so Traffic management and resilience conforms. Add a CI check that every `ruralz_*` name under docs/architecture appears in this catalog.

blocking.section: Observability principles (Telemetry pipeline example) / Metrics catalog (Degraded states) / Grafana dashboards and SLOs (Alert rules)
blocking.issue: Only partly resolved from last round's L1-4. The OTLP example now uses https, but the recommended and canonical configurations still leave every Node permanently degraded, with a ticket alert firing forever. The `cleartext_hop` reason is raised whenever `ruralz_security_cleartext_hops` is above 0, and that gauge counts `client` and `upstream` hops. Security and identity makes cleartext on 8080 and cleartext Upstreams degraded states. The example Gateway in this document declares a cleartext `http` listener on 8080. The Configuration model worked example that operators copy has the same listener, `http` Upstreams (`inventory.shop.svc:8080`) without TLS, and an `http://` OTLP endpoint. The usual Kubernetes pattern, TLS ended at a load balancer and cleartext to in-cluster services, is what Security and identity allows on 8080. Under that pattern `RuralzNodeDegraded` (ticket, 5 minutes) fires on every Node forever, so O3's degraded signal and its alert become noise. Last round's fix asked for exactly this outcome to be avoided ('so the recommended configuration is not degraded').
blocking.evidence:
Example: "listeners:
    - name: http
      protocol: http
      port: 8080". Catalog: "| `ruralz_security_cleartext_hops` | Gauge | hops | `hop` | client, upstream, state_store, telemetry, admin |". Degraded states: "| `cleartext_hop` | `ruralz_security_cleartext_hops` is above 0 |". Alert: "- alert: RuralzNodeDegraded
        expr: ruralz_node_degraded_info{reason!~"state_store_breaker_open|upstream_panic"} == 1
        for: 5m ... labels: {severity: ticket}". Security and identity: "| Client, 8080 | Cleartext, SHOULD serve only redirects or traffic behind a TLS-terminating load balancer |" and "Cleartext, where the table allows it ..., is a degraded state and audit finding." Configuration model worked example: "endpoint: ${OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT:-http://otel-collector:4317}" and "- address: "inventory.shop.svc:8080"".
blocking.fix: Keep `ruralz_security_cleartext_hops{hop}` as the audit signal, but keep `cleartext_hop` out of the generic ticket rule: add it to the `reason!~` exclusion. Add a separate rule on `ruralz_security_cleartext_hops{hop=~"state_store|telemetry|admin"} > 0` at ticket severity, and report `client` and `upstream` cleartext at info severity or on the Node runtime and configuration Grafana dashboard only. Alternatively, raise `cleartext_hop` only for hops Security and identity does not allow. Either way, state that the example and the Configuration model worked example are not degraded under the chosen rule, and add an OQ asking Security and identity which cleartext hops warrant an alert.

non_blocking.suggestion: Each of the two per-Node token buckets is one shared atomic. Under OQ-observability-4 option (a), a client that sets the sampled flag on every request makes every request run a compare-and-swap on the parent bucket's cache line, which adds new contention on the request path. Split each bucket across the S stripes at rate/S and burst/S (target), and consult it with the request's stripe, as the metric shards are.

'A lock-free per-connection random source' cannot be both lock-free and safe when up to 250 HTTP/2 streams of one connection generate IDs concurrently. Use the top-level `math/rand/v2` functions, which draw from the runtime's per-thread ChaCha8 source without locks, or give each stream its own source. State that the 1 µs, 2-allocation unsampled budget includes ID generation.

'offset by the stream ID when multiplexed': client-initiated HTTP/2 stream IDs are all odd, so (base + streamID) mod S with S = 4 or 8 reaches only half the stripes on each connection. That matters behind a load balancer or mesh sidecar that multiplexes over a few connections. Offset by streamID >> 1 instead.

The sharded set is capped at 64 histogram label sets, but the listener and enumeration histogram families already use about 28 plus 4 to 14 per listener (gateway duration, two body sizes, TLS handshake, session duration by protocol, State Store `op`, activation `stage` × `size_class`), so a few listeners exceed it. `ruralz_http_listener_requests_total` alone can reach 150 counter series per listener. Say which hot label sets stay unsharded beyond the cap and in what order, so behavior is deterministic.

non_blocking.section: Observability principles / Grafana dashboards and SLOs (Route detail exemplars)
non_blocking.suggestion: O6 and the Route detail Grafana dashboard promise exemplars, but the Ruralz-owned atomic aggregates have no exemplar storage, and a trace ID, value and timestamp cannot be updated in one atomic step. Specify one exemplar slot per histogram label set, written only by sampled requests under a seqlock or a pooled pointer swap, and add its bytes to the memory model.

A partial success counts as failure and export never drops, so one record that the Collector always rejects (too large or malformed) stops audit export permanently, and the lag grows without bound. Define what happens then: after N retries (target), park the batch, raise a degraded reason and record an audit event. Alternatively, state that operator action is the only remedy.

`RuralzAIProviderCredential` counts only `ruralz_ai_fallbacks_total{error_class="credential"}`. A credential failure on a single-candidate `AIModel`, or on the last candidate, produces no fallback, so the most common setup never alerts. Count credential failures on `ruralz_ai_failed_attempts_total` with an `error_class` label, or add a dedicated counter.

non_blocking.section: Cardinality and overhead budgets (Cardinality budget table)
non_blocking.suggestion: The Plugin histograms row reads 1,600, but three Plugin histogram families (`call_duration`, `call_overhead`, `pool_wait`) × 50 Policies × 16 give at least 2,400, and more for Plugins with several Phases. Recompute that row, the 65,600 and 81,600 totals and the memory estimate that depends on them.

SLO-AI-1 is now a correct good-over-total ratio, but its units are mixed. `ruralz_ai_settlements_total` counts attempts ('Attempts settled with reported usage'), while `ruralz_ai_usage_missing_total` counts requests, and with Provider Fallback one request can add to both. State one unit for both counters, preferably attempts, and align the AI/LLM gateway settlement table.

'streams can pin four disjoint Route name sets for hours' overstates the case. Per Data plane, the closing snapshot ends its streams at once and stays pinned only for the 30 s grace period plus the ending bound. Three sets can persist for hours and the fourth for seconds. The 25,000 ceiling still holds, but the rationale should match.

'OTLP across TB-12 MUST use TLS' is followed directly by 'the Node still exports' over cleartext, so the MUST is never enforced. Word it as Security and identity does, 'TLS when configured; cleartext reported', pending OQ-security-and-identity-29.
